newsitem.title: USA: U.S. plane again fires at Iraq missile site.
newsitem.headline: U.S. plane again fires at Iraq missile site.

text.p: A U.S. F-16 fighter jet fired a missile at an Iraqi mobile anti-aircraft missile site on Monday after the pilot received an indication his aircraft was being targeted from the ground, the Pentagon said.

The incident, in a no-fly zone over southern Iraq, was similar to one on Saturday after which the Pentagon later said the Iraqi radar had not actually targeted the American jet despite indications from the pilot's instruments that targeting had occurred.

Navy Commander Joe March, a Defence Department spokesman, said Monday's incident took place at about noon Iraq time (0900 GMT) about 25 miles (40 km) from where Saturday's incident occurred in the no-fly zone.
The United States has warned Iraq not to threaten U.S. and other allied pilots patrolling the zone, established after the Gulf War to restrict Iraqi military activity.
"An F-16 pilot assigned to the 4404th fighter wing fired a Harm (missile) after receiving an indication that his aircraft was being targeted by an Iraqi mobile surface-to-air system," March said.

As in Saturday's incident, March said, the F-16 fighter jet returned to its base in the Gulf region safely. He said there was no indication of damage to the missile site from the high-speed anti-radiation missile designed to seek out radar signals and destroy such sites.
